paragraphs.en: Audio Ball is a two-player game of listening and reacting. Send the ball to your opponent, then listen for the return and choose the right defence. A successful block leaves the ball with you, ready for your next shot. Let it past and your opponent scores. You can play against another person or a bot.
Headphones help you follow the ball. With the default listening position, you are on the right: an incoming ball moves towards your right ear, while your own shot travels away to the left.
There are three shots, each with a distinct sound and its own key:
- Up arrow or W.
- Left arrow or D.
- Down arrow or S.
Use the same keys to defend. A shot sent with W, for example, needs W or Up arrow to stop it. The sound tells you which defence to choose.

Before playing, open the rules with Ctrl+F1 and choose Audio tutorial. Use the arrows to select a recording, then Enter or Space to play it. The tutorial explains the keys and includes the sounds for preparing a shot and stopping the ball.

To serve, first press Right arrow to prepare the ball. Once you hear the preparation sound, make a separate press of Up, Left or Down arrow to send one of the three shots. A is an alternative to Right arrow.

As soon as your opponent hits the ball, choose a defence by pressing or holding the matching key. You do not have to wait for the ball to reach you. Your choice stays selected, and you can change it with another defence key until the ball passes you.

The stopping sound means you have caught the ball. Prepare it with Right arrow, then choose a shot, just as you did when serving. Your return can be a different type from the shot you blocked. Each return makes the ball a little faster.
For each incoming ball, press your defence key after the opponent's shot. If you are still holding it from the previous ball, release it first.

There is no immediate countdown while you prepare a serve or hold a ball you have blocked. If your opponent takes too long, press Ctrl+W to hurry them. They then have ten seconds to send the ball or you score a point. Preparing the shot alone is not enough.
You win a set by reaching at least 7 points with a two-point lead. At 7–6, play continues; 8–6 wins the set. The default match is one set.

The first server is chosen at random. Service then changes every two points. After a point, the score is announced and a short break precedes the next rally. The ball starts that rally at its original speed.
Press Shift+S to hear the match score, or T to check who serves.

Choose the difficulty in the table settings before the match. Normal is the default. Difficulty sets the ball's initial speed; against a bot, it also affects how quickly the bot reacts and how often it makes mistakes.
- Very easy: the first flight takes 4 seconds.
- Easy: the first flight takes 2.2 seconds.
- Normal: the first flight takes 1.5 seconds.
- Hard: the first flight takes 0.9 seconds.
- Very hard: the first flight takes 0.6 seconds.
On every difficulty, each return increases speed by 5%. A new point resets it to the chosen starting speed.
The table settings let you play first to two or three sets instead of a single set. Every set still requires at least 7 points and a two-point lead.

After a set, the points reset to 0–0. The next set starts after five seconds, with the other player serving first. Whoever opens the first set also opens the third; their opponent opens the second and fourth. Continue until someone has won the required number of sets.
Open Audio Ball settings with Ctrl+P. You can put your end on the left instead of the right: incoming balls will travel from right to left, and your shots will go the other way.

You can also choose the default sounds or the Audiodisc sound pack. This changes the three ball sounds, shot preparation and the sound of a block, among others. The audio tutorial uses your selected pack, so it is a good place to learn the new sounds.
Audio Ball was created by budyn1211, known on ELTEN as balteam.
Up arrow: choose the first defence, or make the first shot after preparing.
W: choose the first defence, or make the first shot after preparing.
Left arrow: choose the second defence, or make the second shot after preparing.
D: choose the second defence, or make the second shot after preparing.
Down arrow: choose the third defence, or make the third shot after preparing.
S: choose the third defence, or make the third shot after preparing.
Right arrow: prepare the ball.
A: prepare the ball.
Shift+S: read points and sets won.
T: read the server and connection status.
Ctrl+W: hurry an opponent who is holding the ball.
Ctrl+P: open listening preferences.
